segments.text: American Fork City Council — Budget Workshop — February 22–23, 2024:

entities.speaker: Cameron J. Paul
entities.remark-context: Police staffing, facilities, retention, and operating costs

segments.text: Police Chief Cameron Paul said AFPD had 54 officers compared with 76 under a regional planning ratio and hoped to add approximately two officers each year. He described shortages in office space, secure evidence storage, and parking, along with continuing challenges involving wages, fleet costs, mental-health services, technology, and equipment.

City Administrator David Bunker said police space was tight and identified precincts as one possible future option, while acknowledging the challenges they would create. He also discussed officer wage progression and said the city was considering relocating evidence storage while expanding the Public Works site.

entities.label: Police staffing, facilities, evidence storage, and retention

segments.text: The workshop compared current staffing with a regional planning ratio and documented specific limitations in police space, secure evidence storage, parking, retention, mental-health support, vehicles, technology, and equipment.
Relevant passages from the official meeting minutes:

Mr. Bunker stated that population affects everything and went over the impact on communities. The next decade will be critical, when the city will see the biggest push in population growth. With the increased population, there will need to be more employees. Today, the city has 293 FTE for about 48,000 residents. The projections show they will need to increase to 323, then 360, and finally 468 in 20 years. With that, space is affected. Staff at Public Works are already in tight quarters. The Police Department has done well to manage what they have, but again, space is tight; soon, they should be able to expand to the 3rd floor which will help. Currently, there is no excess space to expand with the inevitable growth. The next 10 years will be a critical growth period for the city. The city will need another 110,000 square feet to house the employees, and the city needs in the future. One option would create precincts for the police, although that creates a different set of challenges.

Police
Chief Paul explained their biggest need is personnel. While there isn’t a magic number of how many officers they need per 1000 residents, the average is 1.3 officers per 1000. If they use that number, it will place them at 76 officers right now; today, they have 54 officers. He felt their officers did a great job. They hope to maintain an additional couple of officers a year, although that would affect the budget with wages, benefits, cars, equipment, training, etc. In addition to officers, they need space. The department has re-configured every space in their building to fit as many people in as possible. Another need is evidence storage and having secure storage. There is no parking at the police department, with days when they must park north of the city administration office. The loss of parking at the Fire Department and on Church Street will create problems.

Chief Paul stated another challenge they will continue to face is wages. The competition has slowed down, but the city needs to remain competitive. Fleet costs are another challenge as is mental health services, technology, and gear. Mr. Bunker stated they have looked closely at staffing, and if wages aren’t increased for an officer within 5 or 10 years, they can go other places for more money. The city does have a program for advancement for officers, with another option being the step increase plan.

Mr. Bunker explained that Public Works has the same growth pressures. They are working on a plan for a new facility as the current building is packed. They have purchased a few homes on the east of the current building and need to continue buying properties around the building. The plan would be to move the evidence storage facilities and expand the public works yard. They do have a proposal on master planning the space and what the needs will be for the next 20 years.
